hints.title: The Core Recognition Clue
hints.text: Why does standard Dijkstra fail if you only track visited[node]? Because an earlier path to node X might cost less money but consume 4 stops, blocking a slightly more expensive 1-stop path that could have reached the destination within K stops! Thus, the subproblem must account for step count.

hints.title: State & Space Formulation
hints.text: What does 'at most K stops' mean? It means taking at most (K + 1) flight edges. This matches the Bellman-Ford formulation: after iteration 'i', dist[u] represents the cheapest cost to reach node u using at most 'i' edges.

hints.title: The Invariant & Pitfall to Avoid
hints.text: CRITICAL PITFALL: When relaxing edges in step i, you MUST use the distances from step (i - 1), NOT the ones updated in step i! Otherwise, a flight from A -> B and B -> C could be traversed in the SAME step, consuming 2 edges in 1 round. Always clone dist before relaxing: temp = list(dist).

hints.title: Code Skeleton
hints.text:
```python
dist = [inf] * n
dist[src] = 0

for _ in range(k + 1):
    temp = list(dist) # snapshot previous round
    for u, v, price in flights:
        if dist[u] != inf and dist[u] + price < temp[v]:
            temp[v] = dist[u] + price
    dist = temp

return dist[dst] if dist[dst] != inf else -1
```

complexity.notes: Bellman-Ford relaxation across at most K + 1 edge rounds.

solutions.approach: Bounded Edge Count (Bellman-Ford / DP state expansion)
